summary: A report from a UCSB test group that evaluated network resources between January and March 1973, in the spirit of RFC 369. It summarizes the resources tried, makes first suggestions for concise user manuals called MINIMANs, and proposes ideas for future test groups.

plainLanguage.summary: A UCSB test group tried programs and services on the Network and recorded what it learned. The group also proposed outlines for short guides that could help future users.

questions: what is a miniman user manual
subtitle: A UCSB test group's evaluation of Network resources and proposals for concise user manuals.

tldr.problem: New users found it difficult to learn remote Network resources when access procedures and documentation were hard to find.
tldr.mechanism: A UCSB group of novices tried resources, summarized results, and proposed two outlines for concise host and resource manuals called MINIMANs.
tldr.outcome: The report describes mixed evaluation results, suggests future projects, and asks the community for comments and useful documentation.

sections.title: A Group of New Users
sections.content:
In the spirit of RFC 369, a UCSB test group evaluated selected Network resources between January and March 1973. The members were novices in Network use and investigated availability, access, examples, help, and documentation.

The group aimed to produce site-specific and function-specific MINIMANs, or concise user manuals.
sections.plainLanguage: The group tested network services from the viewpoint of people who were still learning them. It wanted to turn that experience into practical guides.

sections.title: Resources Investigated
sections.content:
The report summarizes work with APL, BASIC at TENEX sites, TSO at UCLA-CCN, and MIT-MATHLAB. It also describes a first local user guide for UCSB and attempts to use a local IMLAC for network graphics.

An effort to learn about Harvard graphics access for organic molecule synthesis programs was abandoned after the group received no response.
sections.plainLanguage: Some projects produced useful examples and documentation, while others made little progress. The report records both successful and unsuccessful attempts.

sections.title: Manual Outlines and Future Work
sections.content:
One proposed report type covers online help for a host, including connection, login, TELNET settings, job status, communication, warnings, and references. A second covers how to use a particular resource, including access, editing, costs, sample problems, and appendices.

Future work could evaluate APL, BASIC, symbolic manipulation programs, games, and application programs. The authors invite useful documents that fit the MINIMAN framework.
sections.plainLanguage: One guide would explain how to use a host, and another would explain a specific program. The group asks sites to share material that could support such guides.
